The '''Aes Sedai of Rhuidean''' are two [[Aes Sedai]] that accompany the [[Jenn Aiel]] when they build [[Rhuidean]]. They are the survivors of a group of Aes Sedai who join the Jenn when Rhodric is 17.{{ref/book|4|25}}

==Appearance==
Their names are never given, however they are both completely white haired; one has dark brown eyes, the other "sharp blue". Both ride in [[palanquin]]s rather than walk any distance due to their frailty. At least one wears a blanket over her lap even in the heat of the [[Aiel Waste|Three-fold land]]. Her voice is a whisper, but strong (possibly aided by the [[One Power|Power]], or the weight of prophecy).

[[Mandein]] thinks they are the oldest people he has ever seen{{ref|Their actual age is a matter of conjecture: due to the visions we can trace the number of generations since the Breaking began. Between [[Coumin]] and Mandein are ten generations. Even with the longer lifespans of those treated in the [[Age of Legends]], generational length (the time to start raising children) does not seem to change much. Assuming 20-30 years, that is only 200-300 years. They join the Jenn Aiel in Rhodric's time, with another four generations of travel/building, so 80-120 years for certain.}}, with "ageless" skin so thin the wind might tear it.{{ref|There is an uncorrected error in this book: Aes Sedai should not have ageless faces yet, as they have not been sworn to multiple oaths. Given the age calculations above, their appearance at Rhuidean cannot take place long after the end of the Breaking, which itself lasted 239-344 years. The second of the [[Three Oaths]] to be adopted was made some time before the [[Trolloc Wars]], at least 500 years and possibly close to a thousand years later. Unlike the faces of Wise Ones, this is not corrected in the latest printings.}}

==History==
The ancient Aes Sedai of Rhuidean only appear once; during Rand's visions in the [[glass columns]]. In his first vision they are brought out of Rhuidean by two dozen Jenn Aiel, plus eight bearers apiece for their palanquins. They barely speak during the encounter as [[Dermon]], [[Mordaine]], and [[Narisse]] explain why the Aiel must come learn their true history, or be destroyed. The one with dark eyes speaks part of the [[Prophecy of Rhuidean]] though, when [[Charendin]] questions the instructions: {{quote|The stone that never falls will fall to announce his coming. Of the blood, but not raised by the blood, he will come from Rhuidean at dawn, and tie you together with bonds you cannot break. He will take you back, and he will destroy you.}} It is assumed that she or her companion are responsible for the prophecy in the first place, though there were at least four Aes Sedai with the Jenn at the time of [[Rhodric]] (in the second vision) so it is not certain.{{ref/book|4|25}}

==Trivia==
* In interviews, Robert Jordan confirmed that neither of the two are [[Deindre]], the Aes Sedai with the [[Foretelling]] that Jonai saw when the Da'shain Aiel left [[Paaran Disen]] with their original quest.{{ref/tidb|83|32}} She could in theory have been one of the two who died along the way, though there is not a continuous group of Aes Sedai who accompany the Aiel and the newcomers (in Rhodric's time) are never named nor described.
